Key Research Thinking Patterns: Empirical Hallucination Auditing: Systematically detecting and mitigating AI-generated errors in code generation by cross-referencing LLM outputs against real-world package repositories like PyPI and npm to identify 'package hallucinations' and confusion attacks.

Longitudinal Decentralized Surveillance: Deploying global honeypots (T-Pot) and live blockchain nodes (Ethereum Mainnet) to conduct continuous, large-scale monitoring of attack vectors, credential harvesting, and reconnaissance activities in P2P and consensus networks.

Sociotechnical Ecosystem Mapping: Utilizing massive longitudinal datasets (MagnetDB) and metadata aggregation (IMDb) to analyze the structural dynamics, 'gift economy' motivations, and temporal trends of digital piracy supply chains.

Rigorous Metric Validation via Mixed-Effects Modeling: Calibrating subjective and objective evaluation frameworks, such as Image Similarity Metrics (ISM) and Dataset Value Taxonomy (DVT), using Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC) analysis and Generalized Linear Mixed Models (GLMM) to ensure statistical robustness.
Summary Description: Anindya Maiti specializes in the intersection of AI safety, cybersecurity, and data epistemology at the University of Oklahoma. His research addresses critical vulnerabilities in AI-assisted software development by empirically auditing 'package hallucinations' across PyPI and npm. Maiti extends this rigorous, data-driven approach to decentralized systems, utilizing global honeynets and live blockchain nodes to map reconnaissance attacks on P2P and Proof-of-Stake infrastructure. He also pioneers the sociotechnical analysis of digital piracy through MagnetDB, a massive longitudinal dataset revealing the dynamics of content distribution and 'gift economies.' By employing advanced statistical modeling and large-scale data engineering, Maiti bridges technical security assessments with broader questions of data governance and research ethics, providing actionable insights for securing both centralized AI workflows and decentralized network ecosystems.
